import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 79

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/79](https://www.erdosproblems.com/79)
- [EFRS93] Erdős, P., Faudree, R. J., Rousseau, C. C. and Schelp, R. H., Ramsey size linear graphs.
  Combin. Probab. Comput. (1993), 389-399.
- [Wi24] Wigderson, Y., Infinitely many minimally non-Ramsey size linear graphs.
  arXiv:2409.05931 (2024).
-/

namespace Erdos79

open scoped Classical in
/--
We say $G$ is Ramsey size linear if $R(G,H)\ll m$ for all graphs $H$ with $m$ edges and
no isolated vertices.

Are there infinitely many graphs $G$ which are not Ramsey size linear but such that all of
its proper subgraphs are?

Asked by Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau, and Schelp [EFRS93]. $K_4$ was long the only known example.
Wigderson [Wi24] proved that there are infinitely many such graphs.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_79 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (N : ℕ), ∃ (n : ℕ) (_ : N ≤ n) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
      ¬ G.IsRamseySizeLinear ∧
      ∀ H : G.Subgraph, H < ⊤ → H.coe.IsRamseySizeLinear := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos79

reformulations.difference: The source asks for infinitely many minimally non-Ramsey-size-linear graphs. Lean instead requires, for every N, such a graph on Fin n with N ≤ n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every finite graph can be relabelled onto Fin n, and Ramsey size linearity and proper-subgraph minimality are invariant under isomorphism. There are only finitely many simple graphs of bounded vertex count, even before quotienting by isomorphism. Thus infinitely many isomorphism classes is equivalent to unbounded vertex count. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, problem_rhs_iff_infinite_isoclasses proves the equivalence between the theorem's exact right-hand side and infinitude of the corresponding set of graph-isomorphism classes. Its axioms contain no sorryAx.

review.notes: Checked the sole declaration and its shared definitions. IsContained uses injective homomorphisms, not induced embeddings; H < ⊤ means a proper subgraph allowing vertex or edge deletion. The uniform positive constant and no-isolated-vertices condition match the sources. Scratch proofs verify empty-target Ramsey numbers are zero, all edgeless graphs are Ramsey size linear, R(K₂,K₂)=2, and quantification over Fin n covers arbitrary finite vertex types. Both answer(True) and research solved agree with the current source. The website's abbreviated wording 'all its subgraphs' is explicitly clarified as proper subgraphs in Wigderson's Theorem 1. EFRS93's full text was not accessible from the publisher, but its abstract confirms the definition and Wigderson's full cited paper explicitly restates the original question. The reviewed file matches the specified commit and was not modified.
